summary: This note, drawn from a Wikipedia article titled Adolescence, examines how adolescence affects sibling relationships. It explains that intimacy between same-sex siblings rises in early adolescence and then stays stable, while mixed-sex siblings drift apart early on and grow closer again from middle adolescence. It also covers why sibling bonds matter: they serve as children's first relational experiences and can boost sociability, self-worth and guidance for adolescents.
one_line: Overview of how adolescence changes sibling relationships depending on sibling gender, and why positive sibling bonds help adolescents.
key_facts: During childhood, siblings are a source of conflict and frustration as well as a support system.
Adolescence may affect the sibling relationship differently depending on sibling gender.
In same-sex sibling pairs, intimacy increases during early adolescence, then remains stable.
Mixed-sex sibling pairs drift apart during early adolescent years.
Mixed-sex sibling pairs experience an increase in intimacy starting at middle adolescence.
Sibling interactions are children's first relational experiences.
Sibling interactions shape children's social and self-understanding for life.
Sustaining positive sibling relations can assist adolescents in a number of ways.
Siblings are able to act as peers for one another.
Siblings may increase one another's sociability and feelings of self-worth.
Older siblings can give guidance to younger siblings.
The impact of older siblings' guidance can be either positive or negative depending on the older sibling's activity.
